Arthur Hayes: Maelstrom Has Closed Its Directional Positions, Taking Profits on ETH, ENA and UNI Arthur Hayes said Maelstrom has closed all positions in its directional trading book, taking profits on ETH, ENA, UNI and other altcoins. He believes the market may need to fall before rising, citing uncertainty surrounding macroeconomic and geopolitical conditions. He plans to remain on the sidelines and wait for an all-clear signal. According to @EmberCN , Arthur Hayes reduced his holdings in various tokens totaling approximately $26.08 million, including 8,000 ETH (approx. $19 million), 14 million ENA (approx. $2.76 million), and 323,000 UNI (approx. $2.24 million). — link

Swell Pauses swETH and rswETH Deposits and Withdrawals Amid Abnormally High Contract Exchange Rates According to Unchained, Ethereum staking protocol Swell has paused deposits and withdrawals for swETH and rswETH until it corrects the net asset values (NAV) and exchange rates of both tokens. Data shows that the swETH and rswETH contracts reported exchange rates of approximately 1.203 ETH and 1.138 ETH, respectively, about 6% and 5% higher than normal levels. On-chain analyst Spreek suspected a compromise of the relevant token admin keys and identified a malicious upgrade contract that could potentially impact around 2,500 ETH, though the upgrade has not yet been executed. Swell stated that no ETH has been transferred out of the affected contracts and that the exact cause remains under investigation. — link

Tether's Bitcoin Mining Development Kit Gains Backing from 15 Mining Companies to Accelerate Automated Mining Tether announced that its open-source Mining Development Kit (MDK) has secured joint support and integration commitments from 15 leading mining companies, ASIC manufacturers, and mining pools, including Bitmain, Bitdeer, Canaan, MicroBT, Foundry Digital, F2Pool, Luxor, and Block's Proto. By establishing a unified open interface, the kit breaks down barriers between disparate hardware and mining pools, aiming to accelerate AI- and software-driven cross-platform automated dispatch and autonomous operations for physical mining infrastructure. MDK released version 0.11 at the Plan ₿ Forum in Lugano, with a stable 1.0 release targeted by the end of 2026. — link
